title: New Book by Dr. Jeff Leach Exposes the Invisible Force Behind Personal and Professional Collapse
text:
History is filled with the stories of leaders, families, and organizations that seemed untouchable until they suddenly crumbled. While many point to external factors like bad luck or market shifts, Pastor and teacher Dr. Jeff Leach argues that the true culprit is often a silent, internal drift. In his upcoming book, The Pitfalls of Pride : The Hidden Danger That Destroys from Within , Leach provides a sobering look at how self-reliance replaces dependence and why the most dangerous mistakes often begin at the height of success.
Unlike common definitions that equate pride with outward arrogance, Leach identifies it as a subtle shift in posture. He describes it as the "sin nobody confesses," a quiet independence that convinces individuals they no longer need the same level of guidance or support that brought them to the top. The book serves as a diagnostic tool for anyone feeling an invisible resistance in their life, career, or relationships.
"Pride is the most dangerous sin you can carry and still feel like you are right with God," says Dr. Leach. "It does not always look like boasting. Sometimes it looks like a refusal to seek counsel, an inability to receive correction, or the quiet belief that you can handle things on your own. It whispers before it shouts, and by the time it is visible to others, it has already taken root deep within".
The Pitfalls of Pride breaks down the progression of an elevated heart into practical, recognizable stages:
The Blindness of Success : How blessing and increase can lead to a shift from gratitude to ownership.
The Rejection of Correction : Why highly capable people often stop listening to feedback, turning potential growth into a setup for a fall.
The Erosion of Connection : How pride creates distance in relationships by prioritizing the need to be right over the need to be connected.
The End of Dependence : The process where personal ability replaces prayer and spiritual discipline.
Drawing on historical examples and timeless wisdom, Leach demonstrates that no one is exempt from this drift. From ancient kings to modern leaders, the book illustrates that the safest place to live is not at the peak of self-assurance but in a position of constant teachability.
The Pitfalls of Pride is more than a warning; it is a pathway to restoration. Leach offers a practical guide for practicing daily humility, encouraging readers to return to a life of honest self-examination and genuine dependence.
About the Author
Pastor Jeff Leach is a dedicated leader and communicator focused on helping people grow through spiritual discipline and humility. His passion is to see lives transformed by the truth and to help others avoid the common traps that hinder long-term success.
